text: matched case–control problem handled via ncckl, maps Conditional Logistic Regression Cox model fixed event time uses coxkl_ties core engine. Cross-validation performed stratum level: matched set treated indivisible unit assigned single fold using get_fold_cc. ensures conditional likelihood well-defined within training test split. cv.criteria argument controls CV performance metric: "loss": Average negative conditional log-likelihood held-data, normalized per observation. fold, conditional log-likelihood computed test matched sets using fitted \(\hat\beta\) corresponding training data divided number held-observations fold; resulting fold-wise losses averaged (unweighted) across folds. "AUC": matched-set AUC based within-stratum comparisons. stratum, case score compared control scores, counting concordant/discordant/tied pairs aggregating across strata. Higher AUC indicates better discrimination. "CIndex": Alias "AUC". 1:m matched case–control setting, matched-set AUC equivalent conditional concordance index, computed using path "AUC". "Brier": conditional Brier score based within-stratum softmax probabilities. stratum, probability assigned member via \(\hat p_{si} = \exp(\eta_{si}) / \sum_{j \S_s} \exp(\eta_{sj})\), Brier score mean squared error \((Y_{si} - \hat p_{si})^2\) across observations. Lower Brier indicates better conditional calibration sharpness. returned object structure "cv.coxkl" objects cv.coxkl_ties, facilitating downstream code reuse.

text: function maps CLR problem Cox model \(T = 1\) \(\delta = y\), calls cox_MDTL_enet core engine. objective function minimizes negative conditional log-likelihood plus: $$\frac{\eta}{2}(\beta - \beta_{ext})^T Q (\beta - \beta_{ext}) + \text{Pen}_{\lambda,\alpha}(\beta)$$ \(Q\) weighting matrix \(\text{Pen}_{\lambda,\alpha}\) Elastic Net penalty. eta = 0, method reduces standard Elastic Net CLR. alpha = 1, penalty Lasso. alpha close 0, penalty approaches Ridge. Q = NULL, masked identity used: 1 covariates actually supplied beta 0 zero-padded positions. gives Euclidean-distance shrinkage towards beta covariates external source covers, leaving padded coefficients unpenalized.

what: Simulate stratified Cox PH survival data with flexible censoring, optional binary covariates, and optional ties — sim.cox.highdim
title: Simulate stratified Cox PH survival data with flexible censoring, optional binary covariates, and optional ties — sim.cox.highdim
text: Internal function generate time--event data stratified Cox proportional hazards model high-dimensional covariates, stratum-specific multiplicative baseline scaling, controllable random censoring. Event times generated inverse transform sampling using baseline cumulative hazard. model $$h(t \mid Z, s) = \gamma_s \, h_0(t)\, \exp(Z^\top \beta),$$ \(\gamma_s\) stratum-specific positive constant, \(h_0(t)\) baseline hazard, \(\beta\) coefficient vector. Supported baseline hazards: "exponential": \(h_0(t)=1\), \(H_0(t)=t\). "weibull": \(h_0(t)=\alpha t\) \(\alpha>0\), \(H_0(t)=\alpha t^2/2\). Censoring implemented $$T_{\mathrm{obs}} = \min(T, C, \texttt{max_time}),$$ \(C\) random censoring time drawn specified distribution calibrated approximately match target censoring rate. Supported random censoring distributions: "uniform": \(C \sim \mathrm{Unif}(0, c_{\max})\). "exponential": \(C \sim \mathrm{Exp}(\lambda_c)\). "weibull": \(C \sim \mathrm{Weibull}(k, \lambda_c)\), shape \(k\) specified censor_weibull_shape. "lognormal": \(C \sim \mathrm{LogNormal}(\mu_c, \sigma_c^2)\), \(\sigma_c\) specified censor_lognormal_sdlog. "none": random censoring; administrative censoring via max_time. Binary covariates can specified index via binary_idx. variables generated using latent Gaussian threshold model achieve desired prevalence approximate within-binary correlation controlled rho_binary. Specifically, \(B\) binary \(P(B=1)=p\), generated \(B = (L > c)\) \(L\) standard normal \(c=\Phi^{-1}(1-p)\). multiple binary covariates requested, latent variables generated jointly equicorrelation rho_binary. controls latent (tetrachoric) correlation; resulting Pearson correlation among binary variables constrained prevalence generally close identical rho_binary. ties=TRUE, observed times discretized ties_levels bins (based sample quantiles) replaced bin midpoints induce tied event/censoring times. Smaller ties_levels produces stronger ties.
